{{Short description|Polyhedron formed by capping an antiprism with pyramids}}

 | image1 = 雙三角錐反角柱.gif

The '''gyroelongated bipyramids''' are the [[polyhedra]] constructed with a [[bipyramid]] and an [[antiprism]]. Their [[Dual polyhedron|dual polyhedra]] are the [[Truncated trapezohedron|truncated trapezohedra]]. The bipyramid is sliced into two congruent pyramids and then attached to the bases of an antiprism in between; such a process of construction is known as gyroelongation. The resulting construction has triangular faces, classified as [[simplicial polyhedron]]. There are infinitely many members of gyroelongated bipyramids.<ref name=kumar>{{cite arXiv
 | title = On the Coherent Labelling Conjecture of a Polyhedron in Three Dimensions
 | last = Kumar | first = C. P. Anil
 | year = 2020
 | class = math.CO | eprint = 1801.08685
}}</ref>

Some members are special cases for having [[equilateral triangle|equilateral triangular]] faces, which are known as [[deltahedra]]: the [[gyroelongated square bipyramid]]<ref>{{cite book
 | last = Rajwade | first = A. R.
 | title = Convex Polyhedra with Regularity Conditions and Hilbert's Third Problem
 | series = Texts and Readings in Mathematics
 | year = 2001
 | url = https://books.google.com/books?id=afJdDwAAQBAJ
 | publisher = Hindustan Book Agency
 | isbn = 978-93-86279-06-4
 | doi = 10.1007/978-93-86279-06-4
 | url-access = subscription
}}</ref> and [[regular icosahedron]].<ref>{{cite book
 | last = Gailiunas | first = Paul
 | title = Bridges Conference Proceedings
 | pages = 337&ndash;344
 | year = 2023
 | editor-first1 = Judy | editor-last1 = Holdener | editor1-link = Judy Holdener
 | editor-first2 = Eve | editor-last2 = Torrence | editor2-link = Eve Torrence
 | editor-first3 = Chamberlain | editor-last3 = Fong
 | editor-first4 = Katherine | editor-last4 = Seaton
 | editor-first5 = Craig S. | editor-last5 = Kaplan
 | contribution = Kagome from Deltahedra
 | publisher = Tessellations Publishing
 | location = [[Phoenix, Arizona]]
}} See p. 339.</ref><ref>{{cite journal
 | last = Trigg | first = Charles W.
 | year = 1978
 | title = An Infinite Class of Deltahedra
 | journal = Mathematics Magazine
 | volume = 51
 | issue = 1
 | pages = 55&ndash;57
 | doi = 10.2307/2689647
 | jstor = 2689647
}}</ref> For a gyroelongated triangular bipyramid, it is a non-convex deltahedron because its faces are [[Coplanarity|coplanar]], thereby it is not strictly convex. Considering that each pair of its triangles merged into [[rhombi]], the resulting polyhedron can be seen as a [[trigonal trapezohedron]].{{cn|date=December 2025}}
